title.sub: An AI scientist for physical failures

segments.narration: A walking robot with a hidden fault, and two repairs, side by side in MuJoCo. What if an AI could investigate why a robot fails, instead of just trying another design?

First, how a repair is judged. Every design runs on twenty-four held-out starts the optimiser never saw. The frozen optimiser's repair goes farther on the median, but only nineteen of twenty-four starts walk: a partial improvement. DO-1 changes the optimiser's objective. Twenty-one walk, and a twenty-second confirmation passes. Full recovery, verified. This is purely deterministic optimisation, with no language model, and one replicate on one robot.
Now the scientist: a recorded live investigation by NVIDIA Nemotron, played back, with no new model call. Same robot, a different hidden fault. It barely moves.

The belief engine has two explanations: a weak right side, or a weak left. All seven experiments look equally informative to it. It picks a faster gait, where both predict the same walking. Nemotron picks a slower gait, where they predict opposite outcomes, without registering a formal prediction.
MuJoCo runs both experiments on the damaged robot. These are the recorded measurements, replayed exactly. Nemotron's experiment walks on three of four starts; on one, it falls.
Nemotron's lane now points to the right side, which is correct. The engine alone is 99.8 percent sure of the wrong side.
Nemotron hands the repair to the engine's optimiser. The verifier: Nemotron's lane fully recovers, twenty-three of twenty-four. The engine alone, partly.

Nemotron 3 Super, on Nebius Token Factory, decides what to do next. Deterministic instruments do the rest: experiments, Bayesian inference, optimisation and memory. A hidden verifier decides. The simulation ran on Nebius AI Cloud.

Is Nemotron better? Not overall. A second run made the same choice and only partly recovered. Across thirty-six robots it is level with the engine. Our one pre-registered win is small: six of twelve redesigns verified, against one in twelve random edits, mostly on push tests. AI proposes; physics decides.

end.sub: Built for the Nebius × NVIDIA Global AI Hackathon
